data.text:
How much parallelism does the DAG itself allow when file globs are taken into account, what actually limited in-flight work over 2026-10-01..10-03, and how should ddflow adapt the number of in-flight items safely instead of a fixed max_parallel_tasks?
(A) Replaying the committed log through the real fold + plan() at 49 hourly instants (2026-10-01 08:39Z to 2026-10-03 08:39Z): mean in-flight 1.86 of a cap of 4 (max 7; zero agents in 18 of 49 hours); plan() offered a mean 2.39 ready items per hour because it is cap-limited, and only 1.39 of those were pairwise glob-independent (58%): the offer is priority-ordered and not conflict-aware, so ~1 of every 2.4 offered slots collides with another offered item. Items ready by dependencies and free of conflicts with what was in flight (offered + cap-held): mean 75.8 (queue deep), plus a mean 18.3 held back by a glob overlap with an in-flight item (when agents were running, ~29). A priority-ordered conflict-free fill on top of the in-flight set could have added a mean 24 (min 19, p10 21) items, and a min-degree greedy independent set among all candidates is ~31: the DAG and the globs do NOT limit parallelism to 4. What limited it was the cap, agent supply, and a priority-ordered offer that is not conflict-aware. 39 of 75 candidates at the last sample touch one of 7 hot files (mcp.py 19, config.py 17, api/knowledge.py 11, services/gates.py 10, cli.py 7, api/lifecycle.py 6, core/model.py 4); the other 36 admit an independent set of 25. Glob-blocked item-hours by file (an in-flight item vs a ready one): mcp.py 262, config.py 97, cli.py 91, services/gates.py 76, api/lifecycle.py 59, api/knowledge.py 57, core/model.py 29, services/adopt.py 23, api/setup.py 21, services/enforce.py 20, api/reporting.py 19; the top six files are ~80% of all blocking, and every blocking pair is a file against ITSELF. Among CANDIDATES the same files dominate (mcp.py 3227 pair-hours, config.py 890, api/knowledge.py 852, gates.py 678, cli.py 341, lifecycle.py 294). (B) A safe adaptive controller is: a conflict-aware demand cap, AIMD on a bounded range with hysteresis, signals sampled portably into a git-ignored local ring, plus per-resource admission semaphores for the heavy steps; it only stops ADMITTING and never evicts. (C) Ship parallel=auto with start 4, floor 2, ceiling 8; do not change the fixed default (4) before B-hot-files lands.
Two caps are in play and both are set to 4 in this project's .ddflow/config.toml (schedule.max_parallel_tasks and worktree.max_parallel), and services/adopt.py writes both as 4 into every adopted project's config, so a new shipped default does not reach an adopted project unless the key is absent. The cap is enforced ONLY in plan() (core/schedule.py ~744-780: ready[:slots]); `claim` does not check it (grep: no other use), which is why in-flight reached 7 against a cap of 4 (leases claimed by id, delegated subagents, --no-worktree reviews). plan() ranks ready by (bug, priority, id) and cuts at the slot count, then claim refuses an overlapping glob, so the offered list can contain two items that cannot both start. Hot files serialize because every lease on a file is exclusive and held ~44 min (R-task-time). Signals exist in portable form: os.getloadavg (Linux/macOS; absent on Windows), /proc/meminfo MemAvailable (Linux), vm_stat/sysctl (macOS), ctypes GlobalMemoryStatusEx (Windows), shutil.disk_usage (all); reviewer latency, gate failure rate, merge failures and loop findings are all derivable from the log with no I/O; test-suite concurrency and reviewer concurrency are countable from slot files ddflow itself would write. Reviewer endpoint cost only appears at 6+ concurrent calls (+30-50%, R-task-time), so a count-based reviewer budget is the cheap signal; host load here is ~29-39 on 192 cores (~0.15-0.2 per core) so load is not the binding signal on this machine but is on a laptop.

data.alternatives: Raise the fixed default to 8: rejected, it ignores machines and signals, and 42% of offered slots collide today. Per-signal hard thresholds with no history: rejected, one noisy sample would flap the limit. A background daemon sampling signals: rejected, ddflow has no daemon and heartbeats already run every lease.heartbeat_s on every platform, so samples are taken opportunistically at next/brief/claim/heartbeat. Committing the current limit: rejected, it is a property of this machine at this minute. PID/proportional (PI) control: rejected as over-fit, AIMD with hysteresis is simple, converges and is easy to explain. A single global number only: rejected for heavy steps, a full suite is 48 workers while a review chunk is one HTTP call, so they need their own budgets.
data.consequences: Costs: a new local state (samples ring, slot files), another thing for an operator to understand, tools/list and status text grow, and claim becomes stricter (exit 3 over the limit, force by name). It makes hot-file contention MORE visible, since more agents find the same hot files; B-hot-files and the lease-hold-limit decision (D-lease-hold-limit) remain the real cure for glob blocking. Auto raises the ceiling above the old 4 for everyone, so a project that relied on 4 as an implicit safety must set parallel = fixed. No signal is a guarantee: a reviewer endpoint or a quota the controller cannot see can still saturate; those are covered by their own budgets (B-reviewer-pool, B-review-budget-*, B-quota-*), and the controller reads them rather than replacing them.
data.context: Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'When conflicts are removed you could raise this is - again make it default for ddflow, but also make sure it is configurable by config, cli, mcp so the user has control. Is it possible to investigate flow control options where these limits are dynamically managed depending on capabilities and availabilities - the goal is the project to auto adjust to the maximum that is safe available safely to work : Raising max_parallel_tasks: this only helps once conflicts are removed. Ready, unblocked items are down to two.' Research R-task-time (extended by inv-flow): over 49 hourly samples the DAG plus globs allowed a mean 24 additional conflict-free items while in-flight averaged 1.86 against a cap of 4; the cap and agent supply, not conflicts, were the limit, but the offer is priority-ordered and only 58% of offered items were mutually independent. The cap is enforced only in plan(), not at claim (in-flight peaked at 7). Both caps are explicit 4 in every adopted project's config (services/adopt.py).
data.decision: PROPOSED (operator to confirm each numbered choice). ddflow gains an ADAPTIVE flow controller for the number of items in flight, on by default for every project and configurable on every surface. (1) [schedule].parallel = auto | fixed, default auto. fixed keeps today's behaviour exactly (schedule.max_parallel_tasks is the number). In auto, max_parallel_tasks is the START value (default 4), max_parallel_min (default 2) is the floor and max_parallel_max (default 8) is the ceiling; the controller moves the limit inside [min, max] and nothing ever exceeds max. (2) The limit is DERIVED, never committed: it is a pure fold of a git-ignored ring of sampled signals under .ddflow/local/flow/ plus the log; a clock and a signal source are injected so every decision is reproducible in a test. (3) Control law: AIMD with hysteresis. +1 after adapt_up_after_s (default 600) of all-healthy samples while the limit was actually binding; multiply by 0.75 (rounded down, never below the floor) on a bad signal that holds on 3 of the last 4 samples (sampled at most every 60 s); a 300 s cooldown between decreases; no increase for twice adapt_up_after_s after a decrease. One sample never moves the limit. Only a CRITICAL reading (disk or memory nearly exhausted) pauses admission, and only for that call. (4) Demand cap: never admit more than the conflict-aware independent ready work: effective = min(limit, in_flight + independent_ready). (5) Signals, each switchable under [schedule.signals]: host load per core, free memory, free disk, reviewer latency and pool saturation, gate failure rate and loop findings, merge-conflict rate, independent ready work, quota headroom (when the quota phase lands). An unavailable signal is neutral for decreases and cannot by itself justify an increase; when NO host signal is readable the controller holds the start value (it degrades to fixed). (6) Per-resource admission for heavy steps: a file-based semaphore under .ddflow/local/slots/ with a TTL and stale cleanup, wrapping the full unit suite and slow scenarios (and counting reviewer calls), so N agents do not run N full suites at once; slot counts are configurable and default to a share of the machine. (7) Never evict: a shrink only stops new admissions. Safety floor 1 always; the explicit ceiling is a hard limit; worktree.max_parallel stays an independent hard limit if set, and its default becomes 0 = follow the schedule limit. (8) Operator view and override: ddflow status and brief print 'parallel: 6 (auto: ceiling 8; limited by reviewer latency)'; `ddflow parallel` shows signals and history; `ddflow config schedule.parallel fixed` (or --local) and ddflow_configure change it; the claim command honours the effective limit (exit 3 with the remedy) while the operator can still force a claim by name. (9) Offering becomes conflict-aware independently of the controller: plan() offers items that do not overlap one another or an in-flight item before ones that do, and says why an item was passed over. (10) DEFAULT: ship auto with start 4, floor 2, ceiling 8 now; keep the fixed default at 4; revisit the ceiling (to 12) only after the hot-file splits land and `ddflow parallel headroom` shows the independent set above 12 for a week.
data.title: Adaptive flow control: the number of items in flight adjusts itself inside an operator-set range, on by default, fully configurable

data.body:
Today ready[:slots] is cut in priority order, so two offered items can overlap and the second claim is refused (research: only 58% of offered items were mutually independent). Change the cut: walk ready in the existing (bugs first, priority, id) order and take an item only if conflicts(item.globs, taken.globs, shared_globs) is empty; items skipped for overlap are NOT removed from the queue, they go to blocked with reason 'conflict' and detail 'globs overlap <offered id> (pairs) offered in this plan'. Priority order among independent items is unchanged; when no two ready items overlap the output is byte-identical to today.
FAILING FIRST: tests/test_schedule_offer.py -- (1) three ready items A(p1, a.py) B(p2, a.py) C(p3, c.py), slots 2: today offers A,B; must offer A,C and report B overlapping A. (2) all independent: offered list identical to the old one. (3) an in-flight lease still blocks as before. (4) slots larger than independent count: offers only the independent ones and counts the rest as conflict-blocked, not cap-held (status text distinguishes 'held by the cap' from 'overlaps an offered item'). (5) shared globs overlap nothing. Verify (1) fails on main.
README/doctor/MCP/config: no new knob; update the parallel help topic and the README paragraph on the cap's message; ddflow_next and ddflow_status wording follow plan().cap_note.
data.title: plan() offers conflict-aware: items that overlap neither an in-flight item nor an already offered one come first, and a passed-over item says which offered item it overlaps

data.body:
Create ddflow/core/flowcontrol.py, stdlib only, no I/O, no clock reads: dataclasses Sample(at: float, signals: dict[str, float|None]), Params(start, floor, ceiling, adapt_up_after_s=600, decrease_factor=0.75, cooldown_s=300, quiet_after_decrease_s=1200, window=4, need_bad=3, sample_every_s=60, thresholds per signal with a high and a LOW mark for hysteresis, critical marks), Decision(limit, mode, limited_by, reason, admit_paused). Function fold_limit(samples, params, in_flight_history, now) replays the ring from the start value and returns Decision; decide_admission(decision, in_flight, independent_ready) returns min(limit, in_flight + independent_ready) clamped to [1, ceiling]. Rules: increase +1 only after adapt_up_after_s of all-healthy (every AVAILABLE signal under its LOW mark) samples during which the limit was actually binding (in_flight reached it); decrease limit=max(floor, floor(limit*0.75)) only when a signal is over its HIGH mark in need_bad of the last window samples; cooldown and quiet period; one sample never changes the limit; an unavailable (None) signal is neutral for decreases and cannot justify an increase; if no host signal (load, memory, disk) is available the limit stays at start; a CRITICAL reading sets admit_paused for that evaluation only and never lowers the stored limit; never exceed ceiling, never below 1 (floor may be 1); a gap longer than quiet_after_decrease_s with no samples resets to start. limited_by names the signal that caused the last decrease or the one closest to its high mark; 'ceiling', 'independent work', 'start (no signals)' are valid values.
FAILING FIRST (tests/test_flowcontrol.py, fake clock, hand-built sample lists): single spike -> limit unchanged; 3 of 4 spikes -> limit 4->3 and limited_by names the signal; cooldown blocks a second decrease; healthy 10 min with limit binding -> +1; healthy but never binding -> no growth; ceiling never exceeded for any sequence (property test over random sequences with a seeded RNG); floor and floor-1 respected; all signals None -> start; critical -> admit_paused without lowering; determinism: same samples twice give the same Decision; no oscillation: a periodic square wave of period 30 min produces at most one decrease per 30 min. Verify each fails against an empty module stub.
README/doctor/MCP/config: none in this task (pure core); it only defines Params, which B-af-config maps from config.

GENERALITY (operator: general feature of ddflow, decision D-adaptive-flow, research R-task-time): shipped defaults in the package; works on upgrade (a config with no new keys, and one with the old explicit max_parallel_tasks = 4 / worktree.max_parallel = 4) and on fresh `ddflow init` with no config change; tests in a throwaway project (no companions, no network, no host signals assumed: use the injected clock and signal source); no reference to this repository's hosts, models, core counts or agent names in code, messages or shipped docs; docs ship in ddflow/templates; works for every agent integration (CLI, MCP, and the agents' command files). Knobs are settable via config (.ddflow/config.toml and the git-ignored .ddflow/local layer), `ddflow config --set`, and MCP ddflow_configure; `config --explain`, README and the help topic list each; tools/list byte budget stays green; use ddflow's own fold/plan, never a reimplementation. Machine-specific values (a measured core count, a calibrated threshold) go to the local layer, never the committed config. Hot-file note: touching config.py / mcp.py / cli.py / lifecycle.py serializes other work; claim late and merge fast.
data.title: Pure flow controller: AIMD with hysteresis over injected signals and clock, bounded by floor and ceiling, with the limiting signal named

Create ddflow/infra/signals.py, stdlib only. Protocol SignalSource.sample() -> dict[str, float|None]; HostSignals implements: load = os.getloadavg()[0] / os.cpu_count() (None where getloadavg is missing, i.e. Windows; the controller then relies on memory and disk); memory_free_frac = MemAvailable/MemTotal from /proc/meminfo (Linux), vm_stat plus sysctl hw.memsize (macOS, subprocess with a 2 s timeout), ctypes GlobalMemoryStatusEx (Windows), None elsewhere or on any parse error; disk_free_bytes and disk_free_frac = shutil.disk_usage(worktree root, falling back to the repo root) on every platform. Every sampler is wrapped: an exception or a timeout yields None and a one-line reason kept for `ddflow parallel`. FakeSource (in ddflow/infra/signals.py or the tests helper) returns scripted values for tests. Nothing here reads the log or the config.

Create ddflow/core/flowsignals.py: pure functions of (events or State, now) with no I/O. reviewer_latency_ratio: median seconds from gate.started to the review gate's outcome event over the last 30 minutes divided by the project's own median over the prior 7 days (None when fewer than 5 recent or 20 baseline samples); gate_failure_rate: gate.failed / (passed + failed) over the last 60 minutes (None under 10 outcomes); merge_failure_rate: failed merge-gate outcomes over merge attempts in the last 2 hours; loop_findings: count from the existing loops detector; independent_ready: size of the conflict-aware independent set of ready items on top of the in-flight set, using the SAME selection as B-af-offer (shared helper, not a copy). Create ddflow/services/flowstate.py: sample_if_due(ctx, source, clock) appends one JSON line {at, signals, in_flight, limit_binding} to .ddflow/local/flow/samples.jsonl at most every schedule.signal_interval_s, under a short O_EXCL file lock, trims to the last 6 hours, tolerates a corrupt or truncated line (skips it) and a read-only directory (returns unavailable with the reason, never raises). current_limit(ctx, source, clock) -> Decision folds the ring through core.flowcontrol (B-af-core) with Params from config, and merges the log-derived signals at evaluation time. Callers: next, brief, claim, heartbeat (heartbeat already runs every lease.heartbeat_s on every platform, so there is no daemon). The ring is git-ignored: assert that init's gitignore covers .ddflow/local/ and that nothing under it is ever staged; two agents sampling concurrently never corrupt it; a clock jump backwards is tolerated (sample dropped).
FAILING FIRST (tests/test_flowstate.py, injected clock and FakeSource): two calls within the interval write one sample; after the interval a second; 10 bad samples over 10 minutes lower the limit and the Decision says which signal; a corrupt line is skipped; an unwritable directory degrades to start with a reason; two threads sampling at once leave a valid file; the committed tree has no new tracked file after a run.

Today the cap is advisory: grep shows max_parallel_tasks used only in core/schedule.py, so a claim by id, a delegated subagent or a --no-worktree review exceeds it. In claim(): when live leases >= effective limit (the same Decision plan() used), refuse with exit 3 and the message 'parallel limit reached (auto: ... ) -- release one, or raise schedule.max_parallel_max / set schedule.parallel fixed'; an operator override `--over-limit` records the override in the claim event so brief/doctor can show it; a lease RENEWAL and the agent's own item never count against it; --no-worktree review leases count (they occupy an agent). OPEN question for the operator in D-adaptive-flow (choice 8): hard refusal versus warning. Hot file: api/lifecycle.py; claim late, after B-split-api-lifecycle if that has landed.
FAILING FIRST (tests/test_claim_limit.py): with limit 2 and two live leases a third claim by id exits 3 with the remedy; --over-limit succeeds and the claim event carries the override; a renewal at the limit succeeds; fixed mode with the old cap behaves as the new rule says (documented behaviour change) and `parallel = fixed` plus a large max_parallel_tasks restores the old looseness.
README/doctor/MCP/config: ddflow_claim documents the refusal and over_limit parameter (byte budget green); README and the driver docs mention it; doctor lists recent over-limit claims.

data.body:
Create ddflow/services/slots.py: acquire(name, units=1, ttl_s, wait_s) / release as a context manager, file-based under .ddflow/local/slots/<name>/ with O_CREAT|O_EXCL slot files carrying {holder, pid, host, at, ttl_s}; a slot whose ttl elapsed or whose pid is gone on this host is stale and reclaimed; works on Linux, macOS and Windows (no flock/fcntl dependency); fair FIFO by acquisition time; waits with a visible message ('waiting for a test slot: 2 of 2 in use by A, B') and times out with exit 2 'could not run' (never recorded as passed). Config [schedule.heavy]: test_slots (default 'auto' = max(1, cpu_count // test_workers_hint), local-layer sizing), scenario_slots (default 1 for slow scenarios), review_slots follows [reviewer].max_concurrency; test_workers_hint defaults to 1 and is where a project that runs pytest -n 48 declares it. services/gates.py wraps the unit_tests and scenarios gate commands (and gate run) in acquire/release; an agent that bypasses the gate and runs the suite by hand is not covered and the docs say so. The controller reads slot occupancy as the 'suites' signal.
FAILING FIRST (tests/test_slots.py): two holders and one slot -> the second waits then times out with exit 2; a crashed holder's stale file is reclaimed after ttl; a dead pid is reclaimed at once; release on exception; FIFO order; slot count 'auto' with a faked cpu_count; gates.unit_tests under two concurrent callers runs them one after the other (fake command); nothing is recorded passed when the wait times out.
README/doctor/MCP/config: README and the parallel help topic describe the budgets; doctor shows live and stale slots; ddflow_gate_run documents the wait.

After the five splits merge and a week of use, run `ddflow parallel headroom` on this project and on a throwaway benchmark project. Raise the shipped max_parallel_max default from 8 to 12 ONLY when: independent work exceeds 12 in at least 90% of active hours, the gate failure rate stays at or below the 19% baseline at ceiling 8, and reviewer chunk time stays at or below 3.0 minutes per 5000 characters (research R-task-time). Otherwise record a lesson and leave 8. Either outcome is recorded as a decision with the numbers.
